Reading the columns. BBE is batted-ball events, the sample behind every rate beside it. LA° is average launch angle, EV average exit velocity, and HH% the share of batted balls struck at 95 mph or better. The x-stats — xwOBA, xBA, xSLG — are what contact quality alone says the outcome should have been, stripped of defense and park. Sprint speed is feet per second. For pitchers, every one of those figures is what he has allowed.

Reading the scores. Power, Hits and the leaderboard bars are 0–100 indices built from z-scores across the qualified pool, then blended with the opposing starter as described on each card. They rank players against today’s field — they are not projections, and they carry no price. Rows under the batted-ball minimum are marked SSS and score as a dash.

Probable starters are taken from each preview’s arsenal panel. Openers and bullpen games do happen, and a listed name can change; two of today’s probables (Tyler Zuber, Yuki Matsui) carry reliever-sized workloads, which is usually the tell.

Source: Baseball Savant Statcast game previews for July 29, captured pre-lineup; season-to-date figures. Nothing here is a guarantee. Bet responsibly, and only what you can afford to lose.
